title: Police Commission Of 1860
definition: The Police Commission of 1860 was appointed by the British Government under Lord Canning to comprehensively reorganize the police administration in British India, resulting in the enactment of the landmark Police Act of 1861.
importanceInUpsc: Crucial for UPSC Prelims (historical evolution of administrative acts, Governor-General tenures) and Mains GS-1/GS-2 (British administrative policies, civil services evolution, rule of law vs. colonial control).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of the Police Commission Of 1860 and the subsequent Police Act of 1861.
Evaluate spatial distribution, hierarchical institutional frameworks, and colonial policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions regarding British administrative reforms.
prerequisites: Revolt of 1857 and its immediate administrative aftermath
Crown Rule transition under the Government of India Act 1858
